#### Final pre-grant diagnostic correction

`acquire_owned_work` can persist an assignment before `admit_owned` creates an
operation. If its fixed deadline expires before the first grant,the actual work
can be Blocked while the operation is still Unknown. Therefore pre-grant
diagnostics now emit `WorkBlocked(reason)` rather than borrowing the actual
SubmitOutcome label `Terminal(Refused(reason))`. The Catalog regression advances
the real ManualClock to the acquired assignment deadline and checks both
states; the Runtime regression checks the distinct JSON outcome and absent
execution budget. This is a diagnostic truthfulness correction,no new state
transition.

#### Stop authority through discovery and claim acquisition

The final audit found a separate reachable P2 shutdown-responsiveness hole:
the discovery request did not observe the manager's stop Arc,and the subsequent
claim acquisition used a blocking Catalog mutex without a request budget.
The existing same10s `RequestBudgetV1::until_with_external_cancellation` now
flows through discovery and canonical Core WorkClaimPort/Kernel/Catalog acquire.
No new timeout is created after discovery. Catalog reuses `lock_native_budget`
and checkpoints before acquire commit,so an observed cancellation/deadline
rolls back the claim and immutable request. A postcommit stop skips dispatch
and leaves the original durable retry/recovery path intact.

The final delivery check also runs after commit and lock release,matching
discovery's success contract. A SQLite commit can finish after the supplied
scan deadline or observe cancellation internally; the precommit check alone
would still return an assignment for dispatch. A postcommit refusal leaves
that already committed assignment intact. The added real SQLite commit-hook
regression sets the original stop bit inside commit while allowing commit,
then checks Cancelled,exactly one durable claim/request,zero dispatches,and a
fresh-budget retry returning the same entire frozen assignment even if the
caller supplies a different policy. This is a delivery-boundary repair,no
claim that the existing trace demonstrated a slow commit overrun.

only a typed first Deadline on that scan budget produces scope retry. Other
ResourceLimited,cancellation and storage errors retain their error semantics.
Each control guard's memory scope is cleared after release and rebound for the
next actual reservation. Reserved worker/scope slots are RAII-dropped on every
stop,skip and error path. Existing callers/tests migrate to the same canonical
method; there is no parallel claim API,wire/schema change,issuer or ledger.

## E04/E06 — Catalog observation and original control budget closure, 2026-10-24

Current implementation source:
`cf6a331496cf05f6e4a8cf4b64485292c6f3be238dacedc7059de3c7eae52a5c`.

This is focused functional diagnosis,not a formal performance/release receipt.

### Implemented and independently reviewed boundaries

- Existing Core stage/recorder/schema/parser vocabulary adds `catalog_lock_wait`
  and `catalog_lock_hold`. Wait covers entry through acquisition and post-acquire
  budget validation; hold covers scoped construction through actual mutex release,
  ending before the existing VFS scope cleanup. Field declaration order preserves
  real mutex release before hold-end. Panic is Aborted; errors/cancellation keep
  original product results. Both spans retain the original parent as siblings.
  Off adds no new clock/event/allocation calls,but fixed footprint/TLS/branches
  do not establish zero overhead.
- Canonical `OperationJournalPort::inspect(key, OperationInspectAccess)` and
  Kernel `status` distinguish normal `Request(&WorkBudget)` from explicit
  `PostFailureReconcile`. Normal lookup uses the existing budgeted mutex and
  checks again after reading/releasing the guard. Post-error durable terminal/
  Unknown reconciliation retains its original error priority after expiry.
- Canonical `CatalogReadPort::acquire_ticket` and Kernel `pin_view` receive the
  original WorkBudget. Pre-COMMIT denial rolls back the ticket. Successful COMMIT
  returns the actual ticket even if its hook cancels the request; mandatory
  release or idempotent session custody cannot be lost to a late checkpoint.
  Runtime callers,semantic acquired search and test implementations were migrated.
- Integration review caught a newly introduced context-lifetime risk: attaching
  the issuing request context to a generic retained ticket could retain an
  escaped producer and emit later under an ended request. Generic pin_view does
  not retain that context; existing scoped materialization observation remains.
  The real Kernel regression verifies strong_count1 while its ticket outlives

### Structural audit and selected change

The fresh owned path retains eight distinct entry boundaries:assignment
acquisition,worker grant/precharge,Kernel exact/live entry validation,ingress
birth,physical reserve and confirm,owned admission,and materialization pin.
Existing owned seal/admission is already combined. No further safe COMMIT fusion
was established while retaining current replay,queue/cancellation,physical IO
and fresh claim checks. Catalog object/edge/operation lookups use bounded inputs
and keyed rows;no per-owner global directory/SQL scan was found in these paths.
A duplicated managed live_claim row read inside pin has no COMMIT saving and is
not promoted into a new performance repair.

Allowing an internal interface refactor yields one conditional candidate:
validate_owned_work plus fresh-Unknown open_ingress in one canonical Catalog
transaction,returning the original IngressRef. It could save at most one COMMIT
per fresh Unknown entry,not reserve/confirm or all eight entry boundaries.
Current Kernel preflight runs between these calls. Issuing ingress early would
change cancellation/resource-refusal cleanup and potentially error precedence;
moving preflight early would change authentication-before-work. Recovery,
bounded retention and same-operation replay must be established before this is
an implementation decision. No speculative fusion or speedup is claimed.

A prior durable name plus authentic same-native-FD default full-sync success is
a conditional redesign candidate;current Tracking has no such product credit.
A diagnostic full-sync result cannot supply it. Under the original single-owner
root/trusted-adapter model,a real implementation would still need exact
root/parent/name/inode binding,all namespace invalidation,boot-credit absence,
fail-closed raw fallback/ambiguity and independent restart/fault proofs. The
safe mint point is after the existing parent sync/Core settlement succeeds but
before the FileMutation path claim is released. Core settlement, binder and
directory invalidation, VFS and the vendor's same-FD syscall receipt must change
together;the diagnostic receipt cannot become product authority implicitly.
Native delete-on-close unlinks before AfterClose,so invalidation there alone
would be late. A global namespace epoch is conservative but could lose every
WAL credit to unrelated object creation;its hit rate is not established. These
are design obligations for a candidate,not newly reproduced current defects.
No physical sync or settlement authority changes in this turn.

Instead the original native sync span now receives one fixed mutation-class
counter:overwrite,growth,truncate,create,no_mutation,or unclassified. Handle
history derives from existing BeforeWrite witness/target and BeforeTruncate;
creation follows an actual absent-path ticket,not an OPEN_CREATE flag. Unknown,
growth and truncate remain conservative through subsequent writes. Only
successful original settlement plus lease finish clears history. An absent or
unlinked post-sync witness becomes unclassified. The diagnostic handle lookup
runs only for a matched active scope and before the timed native envelope;
Off/foreign add no new lock,syscall,clock or event,but retain fixed enum/branch
cost. Counter class means **attempt history**,not durable parent credit or sync
elimination eligibility. Native/result and post-settlement outcomes remain
separate;all original error/funding/FD/root/barrier behavior stays.

## E07 sync observer reentry and actual fault closure — 2026-10-25

The next static audit finds one P2 observability defect: VFS BeforeSync,
AfterSync and settlement call a generic diagnostic clock/sink while borrowing
the thread-local CURRENT RefCell. A valid nonblocking observer that reads that
metadata can panic; in unwind builds the native dispatch catches that panic as
a SQLite I/O error. Panic-abort behavior is not qualified by this audit. The
current QueueSink does not reenter, so this does not establish the
cause of the old4K failure or a measured overhead regression.

Only Runtime `publication_sqlite_vfs/diagnostic.rs` and existing
`publication_sqlite_vfs/tests/sync_diagnostic.rs` change. BeforeSync takes pending
state and clones context under a short borrow, then emits/reads mutation/drops
spans outside it. Reinstallation requires the same owner, exact existing capture
session, write-span identity and empty pending slot. Session identity uses the
original `shares_capture_session`; public capture IDs and span IDs alone can
collide across independently created sessions. AfterSync takes pending/context
before callbacks; settlement clones context before entering its span. Off and
foreign scopes keep the original early return, results/fees/authority are intact,
and no new cache, TLS token issuer, metric schema or namespace credit is added.

Four new independent oracles cover reentrant clock/sink plus nested Off masking,
a retained nested Record scope, a reentrant pending handle, and separate sessions
with the same public capture ID and colliding span IDs. Existing normal/error/
foreign-handle/missing-parent/Aborted behavior remains explicit. The initial
